_note: Every user-facing text of the desktop apps, English only. Placeholders: {name} = friend's name, {me} = your name, {time} = local time ("Tue 14:05": a day from time.weekdays and the 24-hour clock; a deadline 6 or more days away, or past, also has the date from time.months, "Sun 1 Nov 17:15", as `raven contact list` says it), {when} = relative time ("5 min ago"), {left} = time left ("about 22 hours"), {n} = number, {path} = delivery path label, {addr} = network address, {secs} = seconds with one decimal, {code} = the old letters-and-digits code, {version} = the app version. The time.* texts build {when}, {left} and {time}. The error.* texts are the engine's plain-English error messages (API.md, error codes): raven-client uses the same wording and the mocks use them now. Keep these texts identical in all three apps; change them here first.
app.name: Raven
app.tagline: Messages straight to your friends. No server.
welcome.title: Welcome to Raven
welcome.body1: Raven sends messages straight from this computer to your friends' computers. There is no server, no account and no phone number.
welcome.body2: Your friend can be on the same Wi-Fi or on any other network. Between different networks, Raven goes through the Tor network: slower, but it works from most places.
welcome.step1: Choose the name Raven shows only on this computer
welcome.step2: Allow Raven on your local network

setup.receive.body: To get messages, Raven keeps a small background program running that listens on your network (port 7420). Only friends you add can send you anything.

_note.network: Keys of the Network screens (network.*, security.*, lock.*, updates.*), shared by all three apps: one text and one set of placeholders per key, checked by check_strings.py next to this file. Placeholders besides the ones above: {addr} is also a listen address such as 0.0.0.0:7422; {port} = a port number; {switches} = lab switch names joined by ", "; {gate} = a gate constant; {state} = a state word; {setting} = a setting's value word; {value}, {how} and {result} = raven-node's or the engine's own word (a radio state, a mapping protocol, the router's answer); {relay} = a relay address and {relays} = relay addresses joined by ", "; {friend} = another friend's name and {friends} = names joined by ", "; {id} = a peer-to-peer ID; {proxy} = a proxy address; {size} = a size such as "12 KB"; {step} = raven doctor's next step; {text}, {coverage} and {until} = the engine's words; {ways} = way names joined by ", "; {route} = a route kind; {connected}, {direct}, {mail}, {internet}, {reachable}, {strangers}, {handshakes}, {bans} and {tags} = numbers. A list goes into one placeholder on one line, never after a text that ends with ":".

network.firewall.title: Windows Firewall
network.firewall.prompt: When Raven's background program starts again, Windows may ask whether raven-node.exe may use the network: choose Private networks and Allow, never Public networks.
network.firewall.manual: If Windows doesn't ask and friends still can't reach you, allow raven-node.exe inbound on these ports for the Private profile only (New-NetFirewallRule in an elevated PowerShell). Raven never changes your firewall itself.
network.way.lan: Reaches friends on the same Wi-Fi, cable or hotspot, even without the internet.
network.way.lanBeacon: Finds your friends again when you or they join another network.
network.way.internet: Lets friends reach this computer over the internet on a port of its own.
network.way.portMapping: Asks your router to open Raven's peer-to-peer port (UPnP, NAT-PMP or PCP), so friends elsewhere can reach you.
network.way.p2p: Reaches friends across networks: directly, by hole punching, or through relays.
network.way.friendRelay: Lends a relay to your verified friends, so friends behind other routers reach each other through this computer.
network.way.websocket: Reaches relays over WebSocket on port 443 where a network lets only web traffic out.
network.way.proxy: Reaches relays through a web proxy where a network lets only web traffic out.
network.way.custody: When a friend can't be reached, leaves a sealed copy with a friend you both verified, and collects mail friends hold for you.
network.way.letters: For a friend away longer than a day, leaves a sealed letter with a friend (kept up to 7 days).
network.way.handoff: Passes sealed messages on between your verified friends, and holds ones a friend passes on.
network.way.routeHints: Friends tell each other how to reach them: relays, addresses and mail friends.
network.way.nearby: Reaches verified friends over Bluetooth when they are close by, without any network.
network.way.tor: Reaches friends through the Tor network from wherever you are, without showing them your IP address.
network.tor.name: Tor
network.way.randomPort: Gives this profile a listening port of its own.
network.way.linkKnock: Stays silent to anyone who isn't your contact.
network.way.linkPadding: Pads messages so their size gives less away.
network.way.lockV2: Locks Raven while its background program keeps running without its keys.
network.way.securityEvents: Notices attacks and odd events, and says what to do.
network.way.updatesFromFriends: Passes signed Raven updates on between friends.

network.portMapping.title: Router port opening
network.relayForFriends.effect: Friends who use this relay see this computer's IP address, and it uses bandwidth for every connection it relays. It helps only while this computer is on and reachable from the internet.
network.nearby.title: Bluetooth nearby
network.nearby.state.held: Not in this version of Raven yet.
network.nearby.state.nodeHeld: Raven's background program doesn't run Bluetooth nearby (an older build, or one without Bluetooth support).
network.nearby.state.live: Raven's background program runs Bluetooth nearby.
network.nearby.windows: Bluetooth nearby is inactive on Windows for now. Windows doesn't say which Bluetooth address it sends from, so Raven treats it as this PC's fixed address and neither advertises nor connects from this PC.
network.nearby.windowsLab: A developer build can try it anyway with RAVEN_LAB_NEARBY_ALLOW_PUBLIC_ADDR=1.
network.nearby.linux: On Linux, Bluetooth nearby works through BlueZ, and only while your adapter hides its fixed address: set Privacy = device in the [General] section of /etc/bluetooth/main.conf, then restart Bluetooth (sudo systemctl restart bluetooth). Without it Raven keeps Bluetooth off, so nobody near you can follow this computer by its address.
network.nearby.publicAddress: Your Bluetooth adapter shows its fixed address, so Raven keeps Bluetooth nearby off. Set Privacy = device as described above.
network.nearby.notHere: This computer has no Bluetooth LE that Raven can use.

network.carry.relayOffered: Friends you lend a relay to: {n}
network.help.title: Helping other devices
network.help.bridge.plain: Passes on sealed envelopes for other Raven devices. Your messages to friends don't use it.
network.help.store: Store: keep envelopes until their next hop
network.help.relay: Relay: relay between Raven's own links
network.help.automatic: Raven sets these by itself until you change one.
network.hideIp: Hide this computer's IP address from your friends
network.hideIp.help: Friends then reach you through relays or friends instead of directly.
network.hideIp.body: Your friends then reach you only through your relays: Raven stops telling them your IP address. Links on the same network (LAN) are not affected.
network.consent.generic.title: Turn this on?
network.consent.carryForFriends.title: Carry mail for your friends?
network.consent.carryForFriends.does: While a verified friend is offline, this computer holds the sealed messages your other verified friends send them, until that friend's Raven collects them (at most 24 hours; letters up to 7 days).
network.consent.carryForFriends.costs: Disk space (at most 128 messages per pair of friends, 64 MiB in all) and some bandwidth when friends leave and collect mail. It helps only while this computer is on and Raven's background program runs.
network.consent.carryForFriends.sees: This computer learns who wrote to whom, when, and how big each message is; over the internet it also sees the IP address each friend connects from. The envelopes are signed, so while it holds them it holds proof of who wrote to whom.
network.consent.carryForFriends.hidden: Nobody can read the messages it holds, this computer included: they are sealed for the friend they are for.
network.consent.friendsCarryMine.title: Let friends carry your mail?
network.consent.friendsCarryMine.does: When a friend can't be reached, Raven may leave a sealed copy of your message with a friend you have both verified, and collect mail your friends hold for you. A copy waits at most 24 hours (a letter for a friend away longer than a day, up to 7 days).
network.consent.friendsCarryMine.costs: A little bandwidth: your Raven checks in with your mail friends every few minutes while it runs. It helps only while their computers are on and online.
network.consent.friendsCarryMine.sees: Your mail friends learn that you wrote to someone, to whom, when and how big it was, when your Raven checks in, and about how many of your contacts you are in touch with. The envelopes are signed, so a friend's copy is proof of who wrote to whom until it is deleted.
network.consent.friendsCarryMine.hidden: Only the friend a message is for can read it, not the friend who holds it.
network.consent.handoff.title: Pass mail on between friends?
network.consent.handoff.does: This computer may pass sealed messages on from one verified friend to another, and hold messages a friend passes on for someone who asked you to.
network.consent.handoff.costs: Bandwidth and disk space for the messages it passes on or holds. It helps only while this computer is on and Raven's background program runs.
network.consent.handoff.sees: When it passes a message on, this computer sees who sent it and which friend it goes to, never the final recipient; when it holds one, it sees who it is for and the friend who brought it, not the sender.
network.consent.handoff.hidden: Nobody along the way can read the messages, this computer included.
network.restart.title: Restart the background program?
network.restart.body: Some of these changes take effect only when Raven's background program starts again. Restarting takes a few seconds: Raven doesn't receive meanwhile, and waiting messages go out when it is back.
network.restart.notStartedHere: This app didn't start the background program that runs now (a login service, a scheduled task or a terminal did). Windows lets the app stop only one it started itself, so Raven will say how to restart it.
network.restart.notOurs: This app didn't start the background program that runs now. Raven stops it if it can; if a login service runs it, Raven leaves it running and tells you how to restart it.
network.restart.pending: Some changes wait until Raven's background program starts again.
network.restart.done: Restarted. The changes are in use now.
network.restart.managed: A login service runs Raven's background program, so this app left it running. Restart that service (or sign out and in again) to use the changes.
network.restart.managed.linux: In a terminal: systemctl --user restart raven-node
network.restart.advice: This app didn't start Raven's background program, so it left it running. Stop it by hand, then start it here.
network.restart.stillRunning: Raven's background program was asked to stop and is still answering. Wait a few seconds, then try again.
network.restart.notStopped: The background program is still running, so the changes aren't in use yet.

quit.title: Quit Raven?

erase.title: Erase Raven from this computer?
erase.body: This removes your Raven identity, your friends and your chats from this computer. It can't be undone, and friends can't reach you here until you set Raven up again.
lock.title: Raven is locked
lock.body: Raven's background program keeps running without its keys. It doesn't receive, read or send messages until you unlock.
lock.notAvailable: Lock while running isn't in this version of Raven yet. In a terminal, raven lock stops Raven instead.
lock.notSupported: Raven's background program can't lock now: it isn't running, or it is an older version. In a terminal, raven lock stops Raven instead.
lock.ready: Lock now keeps Raven's background program running without its keys: nothing is read or sent until you unlock.
lock.isLocked: Raven is locked: its background program runs without its keys.

lock.passphraseTerminal: Set or change the passphrase with raven passphrase in a terminal.
lock.passphrase.notInApp: Setting or changing a Raven passphrase isn't in this app yet.
lock.v2.title: Lock while running
lock.v2.body: Locking keeps Raven's background program running without its keys: it doesn't receive, read or send messages until you unlock.
lock.v2.passphraseNote: Unlocking asks for your Raven passphrase.
lock.confirm.title: Lock Raven now?
lock.confirm.does: Raven's background program keeps running without its keys: it doesn't receive, read or send messages until you unlock, and this window shows nothing until then. Friends' messages wait on their computers.
lock.confirm.doesNot: Lock doesn't protect against someone who uses this computer as you while Raven is unlocked, or against programs already running as you.
